prediction.subReachRound: Model P(team reaches round) vs live Kalshi + Poly prices — the no-draw advance product
prediction.reachRoundNote: Distinct from the per-match 90-min market: a per-team 'reach round X' 2-way market (Yes = reaches that round). Two sources: Kalshi (KXWCROUND, thin in the group stage) and Polymarket Global (Nation-To-Reach, liquid across all 48 teams). ★ = positive edge (model vs the cheaper of the two prices). Real money still gated + $1-capped. The GD (played/rank) column, e.g. +1 (2=1) (#3): group goal difference +1, first parenthesis 'played=remaining' (3 group games — here 2 played, 1 still to go), and '#3' is the team's current in-group rank (1–4). Computed live from match results and reconciled to the official group standings (0/48 mismatch).
prediction.subPriceTrack: Per-contract ¢ + probability at each match milestone (mark-to-market)
prediction.priceTrackNote: PRE→FT shows whether the market confirmed our pre-match pick. ¢ = contract price (= prob × 100); settles 100¢ if won, 0¢ if lost.
prediction.dualUnitLegend: ¢ = the per-contract price (a contract settles 100¢ if it wins, 0¢ if it loses). Our model's ¢ = its fair probability × 100 (the three sum to 100¢). Venue prices carry a ~1–2% vig, so the three asks sum to MORE than 100¢ — a venue's implied probability is the de-vigged price (price ÷ their sum), not price ÷ 100. Ask ≠ bid (spread); we show the mid.

prediction.subBacktest: Model vs sharp market vs uniform, on settled matches
prediction.backtestVerdict: Both model & market sit above uniform — the early tournament is near-random (50% draws), so trading stays blocked. Not a bug; the model is actually better-calibrated than the sharp market here.
prediction.backtestPass: The raw model was over-confident; after probability calibration it beats both the uniform baseline AND the sharp book — now trade-grade.

data: All 48 qualified teams and the full official fixture schedule, kept in sync
Live match feed: score, minute, shot quality (xG), cards and key events
Team strength from world ranking, squad quality and recent international form
EA Sports FC 26 player ratings — every player worldwide, continuously updated
Real-time prices from Kalshi and Polymarket US, plus multiple bookmakers
The dataset grows and re-calibrates automatically after every match
pre: Knockouts are also priced as a 2-way "who advances" market (incl. extra time + penalties) on Kalshi / Polymarket US / Polymarket Global; a Regulation-Time ↔ Advances switch flips every pre-match view between the 90' three-way and the advance two-way (group matches stay on regulation). From the knockout stage, prediction win/loss is scored on who actually advanced; the group stage stays on the 90' result.
Fair win / draw / loss, total goals and both-teams-to-score for every match
A 1,000,000-run tournament simulation → each team’s title, final and advancement odds
Golden Boot odds blending player talent (EA FC), knockout depth and intra-squad goal-sharing
Odds refresh after every match; once the knockouts begin, eliminated teams drop to 0%
Every prediction benchmarked against the sharp bookmaker and venue prices (our edge)
Group matches priced with draws; knockouts resolved by a team-specific penalty-shootout model
Every probability is shown as a per-contract price (¢), and each pre-match bet is marked-to-market (entry→full-time) to validate the read
live: For knockout ties, a live "who advances" probability is recomputed every minute through regulation → extra time → penalties (extra-time fatigue decay + a sequential best-of-5 / sudden-death shoot-out model that conditions on the live shoot-out score).

In-play hedging / risk management: protect a leading position by buying the offsetting leg — the draw in the 90' three-way, or the opponent's advance in the knockout two-way — with a break-even / full-hedge payoff matrix.
Fair prices recomputed every minute while a match is live
Reacts to the scoreline, time left and game state — who leads, a strong vs weak team scoring, red cards, the closing minutes
A library of in-play tactics: goal-reaction reversion, favourite-comeback, red-card value, late-game draw value and more
Real-time value and cross-venue arbitrage detection across Kalshi & Polymarket
Every minute of data and computation is logged for full post-match review
cap.decisionT: Betting decision model (which side, how much)
decision: Picks by VALUE, not by most-likely: buys the side the model rates above the de-vigged market price — the most underpriced one (often a draw or an underdog), not simply the highest-probability outcome
Stake scales $0.2–$2 by confidence: bigger edge, better-calibrated model, and supportive recent form → larger stake; low confidence → smaller, floor $0.2
Sizes with fractional Kelly (¼ Kelly) and raises the bar against the favourite-longshot bias; skips matches with no safe edge
Everything uses pre-match (point-in-time) info only — no look-ahead; real orders are still capped at $1
Closing-line value (CLV) is the primary scorecard (more reliable than win-rate at small N); argmax prediction accuracy is kept as a model-quality reference
cap.simT: IntraGame Predictions (AI multi-agent simulation-framework prediction model)
sim: A separate AI engine simulates each fixture tick-by-tick (≈4000 ticks ≈ 90 minutes) with team-specific tactics, producing a full match trajectory — every player and the ball — plus box-score stats (possession, shots, xG, passes, …).
Each fixture is run 10 times; the 10-sim spread is the implied prediction: the win/draw/loss distribution, average xG / possession / scoreline, and the score distribution.
Each sim is replayable as an animation (a prebuilt GIF and an interactive trajectory canvas), with per-sim and aggregate stats.

A local large language model (Someo Park Local Model 120B, on-box) reads the aggregate or a single sim and writes a concise prediction / post-match analysis on demand; results are cached (7-day, content-hashed).
other: Model probabilities are statistically calibrated and must pass an accuracy gate before any trade is allowed
Strict risk controls: a hard per-order cap and venue-executability checks
A live, match-by-match track record — prediction, bet, result and running P&L
Multi-language, real-time dashboard across every model view
P&L, accuracy and price-track records share one source — always reconciled

prediction.venueGlobalNote: Polymarket Global: read-only data only — per-minute price history (→ price-track backfill), champion-odds reference (Poly side of champion ¢), cross-venue check; US geoblocked, not tradable, no account balance.

prediction.subStyles: Data-driven style taxonomy from intra-game metrics
prediction.stylesNote: Descriptive scouting aid (style matchup carries no validated predictive edge)
prediction.noteCashout: Realized = the decision model backs the most-underpriced side (sized $0.2–$2 by confidence) and CASHES OUT when the market over-reacts above live fair. The Exit column shows when/at what ¢ we sold, or settled W/L; ¢ is the realized result. Avg entry {{entry}}¢ · avg CLV {{clv}}¢.
prediction.noteHold: Hold = the same decision picks held to settlement (win→100¢, loss→0¢). Reference only — the real strategy cashes out.
prediction.noteArgmax: Argmax = bet the single most-likely side every match (the old naive rule). Full-sample reference, not our betting strategy.
prediction.adviceCashout: Once live, if the price spikes above live fair on a goal/event, CASH OUT the over-reaction in the In-Play view (smart-exit, ~67% profitable vs 39% holding) — don't hold to settlement.
prediction.planExitDesc: cash out if the price over-reacts above live fair in-play (smart-exit), else hold to settlement
prediction.planWhy: why +{{edge}}% is enough: the cash-out protects marginal bets (realised 67% profitable vs 39% holding)

note.calibTradeGrade: After calibration ({{method}} {{param}}) the model Brier is {{cal}} ≤ uniform {{uniform}} — TRADE-GRADE (gate passes). Raw model was over-confident ({{raw}}).
note.calibBlock: Model Brier WORSE than uniform and calibration does not recover it — not yet trade-grade (discipline gate blocks).
note.trackRecord: Track record (decision model): value bet the most-underpriced side, sized ${{min}}–${{max}} by confidence, since {{since}} — {{record}}, {{pnl}}$ ({{roi}}% ROI) over {{bets}} bets; {{skipped}} settled matches skipped (no tradable edge).
note.argmaxTrack: Argmax track (reference, every match): bet the most-likely side all {{n}} settled matches — {{record}} ({{acc}}%), {{pnl}}¢/contract. The OLD naive rule, shown alongside so both methods are comparable on the full sample.
note.calibPnlNote: Calibration P&L (fair-odds) is a separate over/under-confidence diagnostic.

sidebar.aboutCompany: AI-powered quantitative investment management — systematic strategies across equities, semiconductors, sector rotation, private credit and prediction markets.
sidebar.aboutParkAI: Default chat mode. Ask questions about strategies, signals, inventory, and performance using natural language. Powered by LLM with access to all data views. Can also generate code, preview, and deploy to sandbox to create custom tools.
sidebar.aboutAgent: Advanced autonomous agent mode. Uses multi-step tool calls (web search, Python execution, data queries) to research, analyze, and answer complex questions independently.
sidebar.aboutClaw: Full AI-powered investment research agent built on Someo Park's quantitative infrastructure. Connects to strategy construction & optimization (MRPT, MTFS, SSRS & AISS), live inventory, signals, and diagnostics.
sidebar.aboutDevBio: Lingxiao was a Senior Quantitative Strategist, Vice President (VP) at Goldman Sachs, holds an MBA degree from Yale University's School of Management and graduated from the Columbia School of Engineering's Department of IEOR. Prior to this role, Lingxiao managed trades in the Equity Structured Derivatives Group at UBS Investment Bank and has also worked with Bank of America Merrill Lynch Group. Lingxiao is the Champion Winner of the Goldman Sachs Global Engineering Hackathon in 2024 and has been awarded at the GDPS 2026 (2026 Global Developer Pioneer Conference, Shanghai) Global Hackathon for an AI Agentic App.

macro.overviewText1: Macro Markets is a Kalshi macro prediction-market paper-trading system: it models US macro releases — Fed decisions, CPI/PCE inflation, jobless claims, nonfarm payrolls and the unemployment rate — and prices the corresponding Kalshi contracts.
macro.overviewText2: Every prediction is point-in-time (PIT) disciplined: models only see data that was available at the moment the prediction was made, so the out-of-sample record stays honest.
macro.overviewText3: The system refreshes daily at 05:00 ET: it updates source data, re-prices every open series/period, ranks model-vs-market divergence, and logs enter/exit/pass decisions with mark-to-market on open positions.
macro.overviewText4: It trades paper money only until the gates pass: the model's out-of-sample Brier must beat the market's, and risk limits (per event / family / cluster / gross) cap exposure before any real money is considered.
